title: Declare It Out Loud
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Declare the goodness of God out loud, bring others into his praise, and take courage: the Lord answers and is on your side.
exhortation: We serve a faithful God, a God who does not change or waver in his thoughts toward you. Three simple thoughts this morning.

First, declare the goodness of God, and do it out loud. There is something unique about using your whole body to worship, not just thinking it but saying it. Read Psalm 118 for yourself this morning and say it aloud: "Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!" That repetition is not an accident. Lies can creep into our lives so slowly we can't tell it's happening. A coldness sets in, and without words we start to doubt the goodness of God. Saying it out loud works on your heart. It says, "No. I'm not going to despair. I'm going to declare the goodness and mercies of God."

Many of the heroes of the faith I admire, including my dad and pastors I've known, would often go away on retreat. I've always associated that with being quiet and still, and I'm sure that's part of it. But maybe it's also so they can loudly declare the glories of God without looking like an insane person: to shout out loud, "Oh, the goodness of God in my life! Oh, the riches and mercy of God!" and have their hearts stirred by it.

Second, look at how the psalmist invites everyone else in. Let Israel say it. Let the house of Aaron say it. Let those who fear the Lord say it. You see this pattern throughout the Psalms: once you declare the glories of God, you naturally want to bring others into it. And it isn't one plus one equals two. When we praise God together, it is magnified in a way we can't manage alone. So gather others into the praise of the Lord. Share this psalm with someone in your household.

And finally, the Lord responds. "Out of my distress I called on the Lord; the Lord answered me and set me free." He did not leave me in despair or without hope. He is faithful, always meeting us in our distress. And the result is that he is on your side. He is with you in the struggle, in the fight, in the hard times and in the good. So take courage. Read the word out loud this morning and declare his steadfast love, so that your heart may be warmed.
prayer: God, what a grace it is to be able to worship you, to declare loudly your praises and our gratitude for what you've done. We have so much to be grateful for and to declare.

When the darker thoughts, the doubts and the distresses of the day crowd out our gratitude, bring to mind what we have to be thankful for. Help us declare it aloud, so that your name would be glorified in all the earth, starting in our own hearts. In Jesus' name, amen.
